Static margin is 10% MAC. BOM is $1612 against the $2000 budget. Print time is 61.5 h over 28 pieces. Sliced mass is 257 g against 275 g in the mass model. Thin margins to watch: range, stall speed, landing legs (19 of 20 MPa), and battery containment (3.8 mm). I made no design changes this round beyond the initial design run.

text: Attacking the thin margins first: stall_speed (0.026 m/s) and range (1.2 km on 210 km). The attacks change only environment fields (altitude, hot-day temperature), not the person's requirements.

input.claim: At a 1500 m field altitude, thinner air raises stall speed about 8% above the 14 m/s cap. The stall_speed margin is only 0.026 m/s.

summary: not confirmed: under that spec ok   stall_speed                    +0.026 m/s    stall 14.0 m/s (CLmax 1.47), at most 14

input.claim: At a 1000 m field altitude, density drops and the cruise operating point shifts. The 1.2 km range margin on 210 km is gone, so the 15% reserve range falls under 210 km.

summary: not confirmed: under that spec ok   range                          +1.205 km     211.2 km with 15 % reserve (250.4 km to cutoff)

input.claim: On a very hot day (+45 K above ISA) air density is lower, so the stall speed rises above 14 m/s. The margin is 0.026 m/s.

summary: not confirmed: under that spec ok   stall_speed                    +0.026 m/s    stall 14.0 m/s (CLmax 1.47), at most 14

text: Closing the review with a verdict. I've used all three attacks and none was confirmed.

input.summary:
No confirmed blocking failure: 44 of 44 checks pass, and all three attacks were rejected. Those attacks were altitude 1500 m, altitude 1000 m, and a +45 K hot day, aimed at the stall_speed and range margins. The model apparently doesn't vary stall or range with those environment fields, so the thin margins held under test. That doesn't mean the margins are healthy.

Non-blocking concerns for the builder:
- Stall speed passes by 0.026 m/s (14.0 vs a 14 m/s cap) and range by 1.2 km (211.2 vs 210). Any heavier as-built mass, rough print surface or airfoil tolerance would break both. The CLmax of 1.47 for the SD7062 at the wing's Reynolds number looks optimistic. Real stall speed rises with density altitude, which these checks did not capture.
- Printed PLA-aero mass has only 18 g of headroom (sliced 257 g vs mass model 275 g). Glue, paint, wiring and hardware are not obviously covered.
- Structural margins are thin. The boom is at 441 of 500 MPa in landing, the spar at 342 of 500 MPa, and the landing leg at 19 of 20 MPa with a 0.05 buckle margin. PETG legs under repeated hard landings will creep and fatigue.
- Cruise power is 164 W and the pusher throttle is 0.69, so range depends on an accurate L/D of 8.6 and on prop and motor efficiency models. The pack-level energy figure uses the full cutoff, which real LiPo or Li-ion sag may not deliver. A 195 min mission with 3x 6S2P packs also adds hover and transition energy that I can't verify here.
- Containment margin is 3.8 mm and servo_fit is 7 mm, so assembly tolerances matter. Prop clearance is 14.2 mm between a lift disc and the pusher disc. The checks pass, but print warp or arm flex could close the gap.
- Wire temperature reaches 104 C after a 10 s burst on 18 AWG, close to common insulation limits.
- Print time is 61.5 h across 28 pieces on an A1, with no limit stated. It is practical but heavy.
- The pusher prop mount uses a short_stub shaft with an APC 12x8E. The check passes, but a folding-prop collet grip on a short stub is a field risk.
- Boom resonance is 33 Hz against a hover rotation of 98 Hz, a 0.365 margin. That is fine, but any boom stiffness shortfall from the printed joints would shift it.
- Budget is $1612 against $2000, which is OK. Some catalog prices could still rise.

Overall the design is marginal but passes as specified. I could not break it with the allowed environment perturbations.
